newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST - S.African PPI seen higher in December.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - S.African PPI seen higher in December.

text.p: Higher imported and local food prices are expected to have pushed producer inflation almost a percentage point higher in December, economists said on Friday.
A Reuters consensus forecast of 11 economists predicted the producer price index (PPI) would grow 0.9 percent month-on-month or 8.7 percent year-on-year from 8.5 percent in November.
The consensus was drawn from a range of 8.4 to 8.9 percent year-on-year.
Economists said increased fuel costs and seasonally higher food prices would be the main factors behind the rise.

"CPI in some ways is a bit of a leading index at the moment and certainly food prices rose more than we expected. I think that will be reflected in the PPI to some extent," said Nedcor chief economist Dennis Dykes.
Consumer food prices increased 1.1 percent month-on-month in December.
Rand Merchant Bank Treasury economist Julia Roy said she also expected higher fuel prices to contribute the month-on-month increase.
"End of year oil prices were still high, allowing for some feed through from the effects of the rand's depreciation," Roy said.
Domestic petrol prices rose by eight cents a litre in December to 221 cents.

ING Barings economist Hania Farhan said that while the imported component of producer inflation was expected to continue growing at around eight percent year-on-year, the domestic component was not falling fast enough to compensate this increase.
The data will be released at 0900 GMT on Thursday next week.
